description: Committee recommends $1.2M for winter warming centres.
$200,000 from city's capital reserve.
Remaining $1M from other governments, groups, donors.
Project budget could increase with external funding.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor DePaul questioned the lack of a detailed budget breakdown for the $1.2M funding.
Salvation Army delegate highlighted increased need for warming centres this winter.
Plan includes separate warming locations for men and women experiencing homelessness.
Administration committed to providing a more detailed budget breakdown to Council.

segments.title: Winter Warming Centres and Outreach Plan
description: Last winter, St. Mary's provided warming for 122-230 people nightly.
Two locations secured for this winter: Friendship Center and St. Mary's Parish.
Expanded outreach by Swaya Toten from Saskatoon Tribal Council.
City requested to contribute $200,000 to fill a funding gap.

chips.text: $1.2 million total funding required for winter warming centres
Warming centres and outreach support for residents experiencing homelessness

segments.title: Salvation Army Urges Funding for Warming Centres
description: Salvation Army emphasized the critical need for project funding.
Noted growing numbers of homeless, already high this winter.
Advocated for multi-level government partnership for robust solutions.
Two separate locations for men and women are a better plan.

chips.text: Salvation Army urged council to approve funding for warming centres
Growing numbers of people experiencing homelessness need support

segments.title: Council Questions on Funding and Operations
description: Council requested a detailed breakdown of the $1.2 million budget.
Administration clarified future external funding would not reduce city's contribution.
Discussion on funding source: RCE versus downtown housing reserve.
New navigation services will be offered at warming locations.

chips.text: $200,000 requested from city's Reserve for Capital Expenditures
Detailed budget breakdown for $1.2 million not provided in report
Administration will provide detailed budget breakdown to council

segments.title: Amendment to Change Funding Source
description: Councillor Dubois moved to amend the funding source.
Proposed using the vacant lot and adaptive reuse incentive reserve.
Amendment failed due to lack of a seconder.

chips.text: Amendment to change funding source failed due to lack of seconder
Councillor Dubois preferred using dormant reserve to keep RCE whole

segments.title: Council Approves Warming Centre Funding
description: Councillor Davis thanked administration and partners for finding a solution.
Expressed concern over lack of stable provincial funding plan.
Council unanimously approved the recommendations.

chips.text: Recommendations for winter warming centres funding adopted unanimously
Motion carried unanimously by council
Councillor Davis highlighted the critical need and lack of stable provincial funding

description: Administration to report on green space weed management, including herbicide use.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
Councillor Jeffries noted Saskatoon has not used herbicides since 1994, and "it shows."
Safety of sports fields is impacted by current weed management.
Councillor Parker raised environmental concerns about noxious and invasive weeds.
Administration confirmed the report will include noxious and invasive weed management.

description: City administration will report on residential security camera privacy issues.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
Councillor Jeffries noted the issue of residential cameras will likely grow with technology.
Residents using or affected by external residential security cameras.
The report will address a 'gray zone' regarding privacy and enforcement of camera use.
